newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares firm on Western, domestic interest.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares firm on Western, domestic interest.

text.p: Leading Russian shares firmed in early trade on Tuesday as investors turned to traditional market leaders and less liquid stock as well as the hot telecom sector, dealers said, seeing the market topping Monday's record close.
No opening figure was available for the Russian Trading System 22-share index for technical reasons. The index closed on Monday at a record 516.63.
"The market is growing in many positions, especially in less liquid stocks," said a Pioneer Securities trader. "I do not think it is just Western interest."
Traders saw interest continuing in regional telecoms on both the first and less liquid second tier, even as it broadened to include other major stock and regional utilities.
Shares in Russia's biggest oil company LUKoil ticked up to $23.10 at 0835 GMT after closing on Monday at $22.85. Regional power company Mosenergo firmed to $1.585 from $1.580.
International long-distance carrier Rostelekom rose to $5.39 from $5.34 and Moscow city telephone company MGTS firmed to $2.40 from $2.35. St Petersburg local telecom dipped to $2.75 from $2.80.
Aton salesman Boris Shvedsky said LUKoil, Norilsk Nickel and Sberbank could see profit-taking by the end of the day but said the market would close higher nevertheless.
"I expect most stocks included in index to close a little higher," Shvedsky said.
